tool_signatures.name: bulk_create_posts
tool_signatures.description: Create up to 50 posts in one PostEverywhere API call (counts as ONE API-rate-limit hit instead of 50). Each post goes through the same validation as create_post, including X Articles, WordPress blog posts (platform_content.wordpress) and Google Business Profile posts (platform_content.google_business). Returns per-item success/error so you can handle partial failures. Use this for bulk scheduling workflows. Irreversible for every post that publishes: it becomes public on the connected social accounts, and PostEverywhere cannot recall it.

tool_signatures.name: create_webhook
tool_signatures.description: Create a webhook subscription on PostEverywhere. PostEverywhere will POST event payloads to the URL whenever a subscribed event occurs (post.published, post.failed, account.reconnect_needed, etc). Each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 via the X-PostEverywhere-Signature header — verify it against the returned secret. The secret is shown ONLY ONCE in this response. Available events: post.scheduled, post.publishing, post.published, post.failed, post.partially_failed, post.warning, post.updated, post.deleted, account.connected, account.disconnected, account.reconnect_needed, media.uploaded, media.deleted.

url.description: HTTPS URL where events will be POSTed (must be public)

parameters.description: Human-readable name for the subscription

tool_signatures.name: get_platform_rules
tool_signatures.description: Get the per-platform publishing limits PostEverywhere enforces: character limit, image and video constraints (size, dimensions, duration, formats), and supported features (threads, carousels, reels, alt text, blog posts). WordPress also lists its blog post fields under platforms.wordpress.blog, and Google Business Profile its post fields (post types, buttons, event and offer fields) under platforms.google_business.local_post. Call this BEFORE composing a post for an unfamiliar platform, or when a post was rejected for length or media format — it is the difference between one correct call and a failed publish. Server-authoritative and cheap: the values are static per deploy and cached, so a platform added server-side appears here with no update on your side. Takes no arguments and returns every platform at once.
